<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds a ROCm AITER FP8 attention path for gated-attention Qwen3-Next-family models on gfx950. One AITER kernel does Q/K norm, RoPE, gate extraction and FP8 quantization, and `ROCM_AITER_FA` consumes the FP8 Q/K/V directly in prefill and chunked prefill. Decode stays BF16.

**There is no opt-in flag.** `Qwen3NextAttention` takes the path whenever the layer and the backend allow it (see Design); everything else keeps the BF16 attention path.

Needs ROCm/aiter#5002, which is in AITER v0.1.25 and pinned on main.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "prequantized fp8 attention", "fused qk norm rope gate fp8" and "FP8 Q/K/V aiter attention". #58713 builds on this PR (paged FP8 prefix path). #59035 quantizes Q to FP8 inside `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass`, a different mechanism from quantizing Q, K and V in the gated-attention projection here.

## Claims

- Prefill-heavy workloads on four models get faster, and the gain grows with context length. At 128K input / 1K output and concurrency 4, output throughput is +62% (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), +60% (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), +39% (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) and +23% (Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B), and mean TTFT is −51%, −51%, −37% and −28%. At concurrency 1 the gains are +28%, +35%, +27% and +16%.
- At 32K and 60K input and concurrency 4: +15% to +27% on the 35B models, +9% and +17% on the 397B. No measurable change on the 2.4T, where these cells vary by up to 20% between runs in both arms. At 60K input and concurrency 8: +22% on the 397B, +13% on the 2.4T (per pass +26%, +13%, 0%).
- At 8K input: +2% to +4% on the 35B and 397B models, flat on the 2.4T.
- Single-stream decode (128K/1K, concurrency 1) is unchanged within about ±5% TPOT, as expected since decode stays BF16.
- GSM8K is unchanged on all four models: paired per question, exact McNemar p between 0.21 and 1.0 over six comparisons.

## Validation


### Same-image A/B on four models

Control and candidate use the same image: vLLM `39983a5e7` with AITER main `285579b6` (gfx950). The candidate adds only this PR's diff. Each run is a separate container with empty vLLM and AITER caches. The 35B and 397B models ran side by side, one arm per card set, with the cards swapped between passes 1 and 2; the 2.4T uses all eight cards, so its control and candidate runs alternate in order (control first, candidate first, control first). Server arguments were identical in both arms: `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion":true}}'`, `max_model_len` 140000, plus `--language-model-only` for the multimodal checkpoints (the 2.4T is a text-only architecture).

**Path check.** In every candidate log (12 runs) the server prints `Using fused AITER Q/K norm, RoPE, gate, and FP8 quantization` and `Using an FP8 context workspace for ROCm AITER chunked prefill`. No control log prints either line.

Tables show the median over the runs of an arm (control → candidate); the node is shared, so single runs can be disturbed, and "Δ per pass" lists every pass. Throughput is output tokens per second; TTFT and TPOT are the per-run means. "Δ per pass" is the candidate/control throughput change inside each pass, which removes shared run-to-run effects.

### Unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_attention_prequantized_qkv.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate_fp8_quant.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_rocm_aiter_prequantized_qkv.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_5_quantization.py
```

Result on a gfx950 card (MI355X, candidate image, worktree at `0dd36cdf81`): 39 passed, 0 skipped. New since the first version: builder gating (`_uses_direct_fp8_context_gather`: supports but is not fed, one layer not fed, BF16 cache, shuffle layout, no layers) and the FP8-workspace guard in `extend_forward`.

## Details

**What runs.** Before: Q/K norm, RoPE and gate extraction produce BF16, and chunked prefill makes two attention calls, a causal one within the chunk and a non-causal one over cached K/V gathered into a BF16 workspace. After: one fused AITER kernel emits FP8 Q/K/V with per-sequence, per-KV-head descales. The causal call consumes them directly. The cached K/V is gathered into an FP8 workspace. `merge_attn_states` combines the two results. Pure decode keeps the BF16 query and the paged-attention path.

**Design.**

- **Capability gating.** `Qwen3NextAttention` takes the path when all of these hold: gated attention, NeoX RoPE in BF16, ROCm, text-only (`--language-model-only` for multimodal checkpoints), `max_num_seqs <= 256`, and the backend reports `supports_prequantized_qkv_input`. `AiterFlashAttentionImpl` reports it for gfx950, head size 256, GQA ratio in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), no soft cap, no sliding window, no sinks, FP8 KV cache.
- **Builder.** The FP8 context workspace is enabled only when every layer both supports and receives prequantized Q/K/V, the KV cache is FP8 and the shuffle layout is off. `extend_forward` raises if an FP8 workspace arrives without prequantized Q/K/V, so a model that is not fed cannot silently get unscaled K/V.
- **No off switch.** Models that satisfy the conditions above change behaviour on this backend. A dedicated opt-out can be added if reviewers want one; `attention_config.use_prefill_query_quantization` was not reused because it is read only by MLA backends today and this path also quantizes K and V.
- **Input contract.** `Attention` and `unified_attention_with_output` take six optional prequantized tensors, default `None`; a backend opts in through `supports_prequantized_qkv_input`. Other backends and models are unaffected. `Qwen3NextAttention._project_qkv_gate` keeps its four-value return because Qwen4Exp's attention subclasses it; the FP8 path is `_project_prequantized_qkv_gate`.
- **Compile.** `vllm::fused_qk_norm_rope_gate_fp8_quant` is added to `splitting_ops` on every platform. It reads per-step attention metadata, so it runs outside piecewise CUDA graphs. It appears in a graph only where the FP8 path is active.
- **AITER.** Calls go through `rocm_aiter_ops` with no import probe. With an AITER that lacks the kernel, the first prefill raises.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**

- gfx950, head size 256, full causal attention, no sinks or soft cap, FP8 KV cache. The BF16 KV cache is not supported.
- Measured on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4 (TP1 and TP2), and Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 (TP8). Not covered: Qwen3-Next-80B, NIAH at 64k and 128k, MTP/spec decode, gfx942, models with a GQA ratio outside the supported set (for example the Qwen3.6/3.8 27B dense models, ratio 6, keep the BF16 path).
- CI: the MI300 mirror runs the unit tests, which mock the AITER kernels. The gfx950 kernels are exercised only by the end-to-end runs above.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import attention as attention_module
+from vllm.v1.attention.backend import PrequantizedQKV
+
+# (tokens, query heads, KV heads, head size) as seen by one rank: decode, an odd
+# mixed batch and a full prefill chunk, over the GQA ratios the backend admits
+# (TP1 to TP8 of a 16-query-head, 2-KV-head model, and a single KV head).
+WORKLOADS = pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("tokens", "num_heads", "num_kv_heads", "head_size"),
+    [
+        pytest.param(1, 16, 2, 256, id="decode-tp1"),
+        pytest.param(7, 8, 1, 256, id="mixed-tp2"),
+        pytest.param(129, 4, 1, 256, id="mixed-tp4"),
+        pytest.param(2048, 16, 1, 256, id="chunk-ratio16"),
+    ],
+)
+
+
+def _make_tensors(tokens, num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size):
+    num_seqs = max(1, tokens // 4)
+    return (
+        torch.randn(tokens, num_heads, head_size),
+        torch.randn(tokens, num_kv_heads, head_size),
+        torch.randn(tokens, num_kv_heads, head_size),
+        torch.randn(num_seqs, num_kv_heads),
+        torch.randn(num_seqs, num_kv_heads),
+        torch.randn(num_seqs, num_kv_heads),
+    )
+
+
+def test_make_prequantized_qkv_requires_all_tensors():
+    assert (
+        attention_module._make_prequantized_qkv(None, None, None, None, None, None)
+        is None
+    )
+
+    tensors = _make_tensors(2, 4, 1, 8)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires query, key, value"):
+        attention_module._make_prequantized_qkv(
+            tensors[0], tensors[1], tensors[2], tensors[3], tensors[4], None
+        )
+
+
+@WORKLOADS
+def test_make_prequantized_qkv_preserves_tensor_identity(
+    tokens, num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size
+):
+    tensors = _make_tensors(tokens, num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size)
+    result = attention_module._make_prequantized_qkv(*tensors)
+
+    assert isinstance(result, PrequantizedQKV)
+    assert all(actual is expected for actual, expected in zip(result, tensors))
+
+
+class _RecordingAttentionImpl:
+    def __init__(self, supports_prequantized_qkv_input: bool):
+        self.supports_prequantized_qkv_input = supports_prequantized_qkv_input
+        self.standard_calls = 0
+        self.prequantized_calls = 0
+        self.received_prequantized_qkv: PrequantizedQKV | None = None
+
+    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        self.standard_calls += 1
+
+    def forward_with_prequantized_qkv(
+        self, *args, prequantized_qkv: PrequantizedQKV, **kwargs
+    ):
+        self.prequantized_calls += 1
+        self.received_prequantized_qkv = prequantized_qkv
+
+
+def _patch_attention_context(monkeypatch, impl):
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(impl=impl)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        attention_module,
+        "get_attention_context",
+        lambda layer_name: (object(), layer, torch.empty(0), None),
+    )
+
+
+@WORKLOADS
+def test_unified_attention_dispatches_prequantized_qkv(
+    monkeypatch, tokens, num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size
+):
+    impl = _RecordingAttentionImpl(supports_prequantized_qkv_input=True)
+    _patch_attention_context(monkeypatch, impl)
+    tensors = _make_tensors(tokens, num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size)
+
+    attention_module.unified_attention_with_output(
+        tensors[0],
+        tensors[1],
+        tensors[2],
+        torch.empty_like(tensors[0]),
+        "layer",
+        prequantized_query=tensors[0],
+        prequantized_key=tensors[1],
+        prequantized_value=tensors[2],
+        prequantized_query_descale=tensors[3],
+        prequantized_key_descale=tensors[4],
+        prequantized_value_descale=tensors[5],
+    )
+
+    assert impl.standard_calls == 0
+    assert impl.prequantized_calls == 1
+    assert impl.received_prequantized_qkv is not None
+    assert all(
+        actual is expected
+        for actual, expected in zip(impl.received_prequantized_qkv, tensors)
+    )
+
+
+def test_unified_attention_custom_op_schema_has_prequantized_qkv():
+    schema = str(torch.ops.vllm.unified_attention_with_output.default._schema)
+
+    for argument in (
+        "prequantized_query",
+        "prequantized_key",
+        "prequantized_value",
+        "prequantized_query_descale",
+        "prequantized_key_descale",
+        "prequantized_value_descale",
+    ):
+        assert f"Tensor? {argument}=None" in schema
+
+
+def test_unified_attention_rejects_unsupported_prequantized_qkv(monkeypatch):
+    impl = _RecordingAttentionImpl(supports_prequantized_qkv_input=False)
+    _patch_attention_context(monkeypatch, impl)
+    tensors = _make_tensors(2, 4, 1, 8)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="does not support prequantized QKV"):
+        attention_module.unified_attention_with_output(
+            tensors[0],
+            tensors[1],
+            tensors[2],
+            torch.empty_like(tensors[0]),
+            "layer",
+            prequantized_query=tensors[0],
+            prequantized_key=tensors[1],
+            prequantized_value=tensors[2],
+            prequantized_query_descale=tensors[3],
+            prequantized_key_descale=tensors[4],
+            prequantized_value_descale=tensors[5],
+        )
+
+    assert impl.standard_calls == 0
+    assert impl.prequantized_calls == 0
+
+
+def test_unified_attention_standard_path_is_unchanged(monkeypatch):
+    impl = _RecordingAttentionImpl(supports_prequantized_qkv_input=False)
+    _patch_attention_context(monkeypatch, impl)
+    query, key, value, *_ = _make_tensors(2, 4, 1, 8)
+
+    attention_module.unified_attention_with_output(
+        query,
+        key,
+        value,
+        torch.empty_like(query),
+        "layer",
+    )
+
+    assert impl.standard_calls == 1
+    assert impl.prequantized_calls == 0

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.utils import opcheck
+from vllm.model_executor.layers import (
+    fused_qk_norm_rope_gate_fp8_quant as prep_module,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import attention as attention_module
+from vllm.model_executor.models import qwen3_next as qwen3_next_model
+from vllm.v1.attention.backend import PrequantizedQKV
+
+HEAD_DIM = 256
+ROTARY_DIM = 64
+MAX_NUM_SEQS = 256
+
+# Query and KV heads per rank for a 16-query-head, 2-KV-head model at TP1, TP2
+# and TP4 (KV heads replicate once TP exceeds them). All have a GQA ratio the
+# backend admits.
+HEADS = pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("num_heads", "num_kv_heads"),
+    [(16, 2), (8, 1), (4, 1)],
+    ids=["tp1", "tp2", "tp4"],
+)

+def _native_qk_gate(inputs, heads, kv_heads):
+    """Gemma RMSNorm (1 + w) and NeoX RoPE in fp32, plus the gate."""
+    q_gate, key, _, query_weight, key_weight, cos_sin_cache, positions = inputs
+    rows = q_gate.shape[0]
+    q_and_gate = q_gate.view(rows, heads, 2, HEAD_DIM).float()
+    query, gate = q_and_gate[:, :, 0], q_and_gate[:, :, 1]
+    key = key.view(rows, kv_heads, HEAD_DIM).float()
+
+    def norm(x, weight):
+        variance = x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
+        return x * torch.rsqrt(variance + EPS) * (1.0 + weight.float())
+
+    cos, sin = cos_sin_cache[positions].float().chunk(2, dim=-1)
+
+    def rope(x):
+        x1, x2 = x[..., : ROTARY_DIM // 2], x[..., ROTARY_DIM // 2 : ROTARY_DIM]
+        c, s = cos[:, None, :], sin[:, None, :]
+        return torch.cat((x1 * c - x2 * s, x2 * c + x1 * s, x[..., ROTARY_DIM:]), -1)
+
+    return rope(norm(query, query_weight)), rope(norm(key, key_weight)), gate
+

+def _dequantize(fp8, descale, first_sequence, starts, kv_heads):
+    """fp8 (tokens, heads, D) with one descale per (sequence, KV head)."""
+    values = fp8.float()
+    group = fp8.shape[1] // kv_heads
+    for seq in range(len(starts) - 1):
+        rows = slice(starts[seq], starts[seq + 1])
+        for kv_head in range(kv_heads):
+            heads = slice(kv_head * group, (kv_head + 1) * group)
+            values[rows, heads] *= descale[first_sequence + seq, kv_head]
+    return values

+    _resolve_layer_name,
+    direct_register_custom_op,
+)
+

+

+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+]

+    q_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    key: torch.Tensor,
+    value: torch.Tensor,
+    num_query_heads: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+) -> tuple[
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+    torch.Tensor,
+]:
+    total_tokens = q_gate.shape[0]
+    fp8_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
+    query_fp8 = torch.empty(
+        (total_tokens, num_query_heads, head_dim),
+        dtype=fp8_dtype,
+        device=q_gate.device,
+    )
+    key_fp8 = torch.empty(
+        (total_tokens, num_kv_heads, head_dim),
+        dtype=fp8_dtype,
+        device=key.device,
+    )
+    value_fp8 = torch.empty(
+        (total_tokens, num_kv_heads, head_dim),
+        dtype=fp8_dtype,
+        device=value.device,
+    )
+    query_descale = torch.empty(
+        (MAX_PREQUANTIZED_SEQUENCES, num_kv_heads),
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device=q_gate.device,
+    )
+    key_descale = torch.empty_like(query_descale)
+    value_descale = torch.empty_like(query_descale)
+    return (
+        query_fp8,
+        key_fp8,
+        value_fp8,
+        query_descale,
+        key_descale,
+        value_descale,
+    )
+
+
+def _qwen3_next_fp8_qkv_prep_impl(
+    q_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    key: torch.Tensor,
+    value: torch.Tensor,
+    query_norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    key_norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    layer_name: LayerNameType,
+    eps: float,
+    num_query_heads: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    rotary_dim: int,
+) -> Qwen3NextFp8PrepOutputs:
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.attention import (
+        get_attention_context,
+    )
+
+    resolved_name = _resolve_layer_name(layer_name)
+    attn_metadata, _, _, _ = get_attention_context(resolved_name)
+    total_tokens = q_gate.shape[0]
+    if attn_metadata is None:
+        num_actual_tokens = total_tokens
+        cu_seqlens = (
+            torch.arange(
+                2,
+                dtype=torch.int32,
+                device=q_gate.device,
+            )
+            * total_tokens
+        )
+        quant_token_start = 0
+        quant_sequence_start = 0
+    else:
+        num_actual_tokens = int(attn_metadata.num_actual_tokens)
+        cu_seqlens = attn_metadata.query_start_loc
+        num_decodes = int(getattr(attn_metadata, "num_decodes", 0))
+        quant_token_start = int(getattr(attn_metadata, "num_decode_tokens", 0))
+        quant_sequence_start = num_decodes
+
+    if quant_token_start == num_actual_tokens:
+        query, output_key, gate = fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate(
+            q_gate,
+            key,
+            query_norm_weight.float() + 1.0,
+            key_norm_weight.float() + 1.0,
+            cos_sin_cache,
+            positions,
+            eps,
+            num_query_heads,
+            num_kv_heads,
+            head_dim,
+            rotary_dim,
+        )
+        return (
+            query,
+            output_key,
+            gate,
+            *_allocate_prequantized_outputs(
+                q_gate,
+                key,
+                value,
+                num_query_heads,
+                num_kv_heads,
+                head_dim,
+            ),
+        )

@nholmber @mjkvaak-amd this per-sequence descale is not applied by AITER. With AITER v0.1.26 (the version pinned on main), the FP8 hd256 varlen kernel (`fmha_v3_varlen_fwd` → `fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_group`) reads only `descale[0, 0]`. The `(batch, num_kv_heads)` shape passes AITER's `is_fmha_v3_fp8()` check, but every sequence after the first and every KV head after the first gets scaled with the first entry.

Checked on MI355X (gfx950) with FP8 Q/K/V quantized per (sequence, KV head), comparing against BF16 attention on the same FP8 values dequantized with their own descales:

| case | per-(seq, KV head) descales | one global descale |
|---|---|---|
| 4 q / 1 kv, seqs (300, 129, 2, 1000) | 79% rel. error | 1.0% |
| 32 q / 2 kv, one seq of 2048 | 44% | 0.9% |
| 16 q / 2 kv, seqs (500, 700) | 82% | 1.0% |

Thank you for reviewing, Simon! 🙏 

**Question 1: **

* `supports_quant_query_input `quantizes only Q, with a static `_q_scale` (1.0 for these checkpoints), but this path also needs FP8 K and V with per-sequence, per-head descales for all three. 
* The `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` pass doesn't match gated layers, because they chunk `q_gate` first and take the eager path on ROCm. Its ROCm hook also returns K dequantized to BF16, and the pass is disabled under default flags (both A/B arms log "Disabling fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache"). 
* Either way, the backend changes and the `Attention` kwargs stay, so a pass-based version would only move the `qwen3_next.py` part into a compile-only pattern. 

Finally, and importantly, this PR is built around AITER's `fused_qk_norm_rope_and_cache` kernel, which writes the KV cache and has no gate or FP8 Q/K/V outputs. This kernel is from ROCm/aiter#5002, and is cache-independent by design.

Major issue AI found out after removing the gating env variable:
> The backend and the model decide separately whether the FP8 path is on.
> - Backend: the builder makes the chunked-prefill context workspace FP8 if every layer's impl is capable: gfx950, head size 256, FP8 KV cache (rocm_aiter_fa.py:477-508).
> - Model: it sends FP8 Q/K/V only if it opts in: the exact Qwen3.8-2.4T config, text-only, max_num_seqs ≤ 256 (qwen3_next.py:421-430).
> 
> The removed env flag used to keep the two in sync. Now, whenever a layer is capable but the model declines, extend_forward gathers cached K/V into the FP8 workspace and calls CK with a BF16 query and FP8 K/V. CK rejects that on the first batch with cached context (a chunked prefill or a prefix hit).
> 
> That covers:
> - the target model with the default max_num_seqs (1024 on MI355X, which includes the description's serve command);
> - other Qwen3.5/3.8/Qwen3-Next models with FP8 KV on ROCM_AITER_FA.

> # qwen3_next.py, after computing use_prequantized_qkv

> ```

> The model is built before the builder, so the flag is always set in time, and every other model keeps the BF16 workspace. Add a builder test: capable impl plus FP8 KV, but the model hasn't opted in, so the workspace is BF16.
